name: Avodah Zarah (Idol Worship — General Prohibitions)
notes: General prohibitions related to idol worship including business dealings, selling items, and benefiting from idols

name: Commerce Near Gentile Festivals
hebrew: אסור לשאת ולתת עם הגוים לפני אידיהם
notes: Prohibition on conducting business with gentiles in the days before their festivals, lest they give thanks to their idols

name: Selling Items to Gentiles (Issurei Mechirah)
notes: Prohibitions on selling certain items to gentiles including animals, weapons, and items used for idol worship

name: Selling Large Animals to Gentiles
notes: Prohibition against selling large domesticated animals to gentiles lest they cause the Jew's animal to perform labor on Shabbat

name: Renting Property to Gentiles
notes: Laws governing renting houses and fields to gentiles in Eretz Yisrael, Syria, and outside Israel, due to concerns about idol worship and land settlement

name: Nullification of Idols (Bitul Avodah Zarah)
notes: Laws governing how an idol's forbidden status is revoked, including who can nullify it and what acts constitute nullification

name: Benefit from Idolatry (Hanaah min Avodah Zarah)
notes: Prohibition on deriving any benefit from objects of idol worship, their accessories, and items that served idol worship

name: Ashera (Idolatrous Tree)
notes: Laws of trees planted or used for idol worship, including their forbidden status, benefit from their shade, and nullification

name: Markulis (Mercury Idol)
notes: Laws specific to the Mercury idol worshipped by stone-casting, including which stones near it are forbidden

name: Statues (Tzlamim) and Idolatrous Images
notes: Laws regarding statues and images assumed to be idols, what makes them forbidden, and fragments of statues

name: Wine Used for Libation — Detailed Laws (Yayin Nesech)
notes: Detailed halakhot of wine used for idolatrous libations: touch by gentile, mixture, safeguarding, supervision, and nullification in mixture

name: Gentile Wine — Detailed Laws (Stam Yeinam)
notes: Detailed laws of ordinary gentile wine: supervision, temporary absence, placement in public domain, and wage from wine work

name: Bishul Akum — Detailed Laws
notes: Boiled and pickled vegetables prepared by gentiles and their prohibited status

name: Reason for Prohibition of Gentile Cheese
notes: Talmudic discussion of the reasons behind the prohibition of gentile cheese, including curdling with carcass stomach or stomach of calf used for idol worship

name: Milk Milked by Gentile — Supervision Requirement
notes: Requirement for Jewish supervision when a gentile milks an animal, and status of milk without such supervision

name: Fish Brine and Certain Foods from Gentiles
notes: Laws of specific foods from gentiles such as fish brine, cheese of Beit Unyaki, and their level of prohibition

name: Mixtures Involving Wine Used for Libation
notes: Rules for how wine used for libation renders mixtures forbidden — same species forbidden with any amount; different species only if flavor is imparted

name: Mixtures Involving Idolatrous Items
notes: List of forbidden items that in any amount render their mixture forbidden, including idols, condemned ox, broken-necked heifer, and others

name: Kashering Utensils Purchased from Gentiles
notes: Process of immersion, purging with boiling water, or heating until white-hot for utensils purchased from gentiles, based on how they were used

name: Immersion of Vessels Purchased from Gentiles
notes: Requirement to immerse vessels purchased from gentiles in a mikvah before use

name: Seclusion with Gentiles (Yichud im Nochri)
notes: Prohibition on a Jewish woman secluding herself with gentile men due to fear of sexual assault, and any person with gentiles due to fear of bloodshed

name: Leaving Animals with Gentiles
notes: Prohibition on keeping animals in gentile inns due to suspicion of bestiality

name: Jewish Midwife Assisting Gentile Birth
notes: Prohibition on a Jewish woman delivering a gentile child as she would be aiding the birth of an idolater; permitted in the reverse

name: Nursing by Gentile Woman
notes: Conditions under which a gentile woman may nurse a Jewish child and restrictions on Jewish woman nursing a gentile child

name: Haircut from a Gentile
notes: Prohibition on receiving a haircut from a gentile due to danger, with dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbis regarding public thoroughfare

name: Winepress Owned or Used by Gentile
notes: Laws of purchasing or using a winepress in which a gentile has trodden, including when the juice acquires the status of forbidden wine

name: Wine Left Unattended with Gentile
notes: Rules for how long a Jew may be absent from wine in the presence of a gentile before it becomes forbidden as wine used for libation

name: Items That Cannot Be Nullified (Lo Batel)
notes: Specific list of items such as idols, yayin nesech, and others that render any mixture forbidden regardless of proportion

name: Impurity Transmitted by Idolatrous Objects Through Carrying
notes: Dispute whether objects of idol worship transmit impurity like a creeping animal (by touch) or like a menstruating woman (by carrying)

name: Building for Idol Worship
notes: Prohibition on assisting in building structures used for idol worship such as basilicas, tribunals, and stadiums

name: Accessories of Idol Worship (Mishimshei Avodah Zarah)
notes: Forbidden status of items used as accessories for idol worship and how nullification of the idol affects its accessories

name: Wages from Work Involving Idolatrous Wine or Items
notes: Whether wages earned by a Jew for transporting or handling wine used for libation are forbidden

name: Idols Abandoned in Peacetime vs. Wartime
notes: Distinction between idols abandoned voluntarily in peacetime (permitted) vs. in wartime under duress (prohibited)

name: Gentile's Own Idol — Immediate Prohibition
hebrew: עבודה זרה של גוי אסורה מיד
notes: A gentile's idol is forbidden immediately upon its fashioning; a Jew's idol only becomes forbidden upon actual worship

name: Idolatry Laws Specific to Eretz Yisrael
notes: Special stringencies in Eretz Yisrael regarding renting to gentiles, land settlement, and avoiding support of idolatry on holy land

name: Wine Cistern Contaminated by Libation Wine
notes: Wine used for libation that fell into a cistern renders all wine forbidden; dispute about selling the whole and deducting the value of the forbidden portion
